root_cause.text: The Microchip core-QSPI driver incorrectly used its normal write-read transmit path for emulated read-only dual/quad SPI transfers, causing it to send dummy data when the hardware core itself should have generated the read clock cycles.
root_cause.evidence: In `mchp_coreqspi_transfer_one()`, the old code treated any transfer with `rx_buf` as `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op(qspi)`, but the patch adds a `dual_quad` check for `SPI_NBITS_DUAL/QUAD` and diverts those cases to `mchp_coreqspi_read_op(qspi)` instead, matching the commit message stating “don't attempt to transmit during emulated read-only dual/quad operations” because “the core will deal with reads by creating clock cycles itself.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Route DUAL/QUAD SPI transfers to the proper read path instead of the combined write-read path.
intent_record.what: The function `mchp_coreqspi_transfer_one()` now declares a local `bool dual_quad = false;` and sets it to true when any transfer direction uses QUAD or DUAL bus widths (`tx_nbits` or `rx_nbits`). The receive path is split: when `t->rx_buf` is present and `dual_quad` is false, it continues to call `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op(qspi)`, but when `dual_quad` is true it instead calls `mchp_coreqspi_read_op(qspi)` after assigning `rxbuf` and `rx_len`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, transfers that use dual- or quad-width SPI signaling are routed through a dedicated read operation instead of the combined write-read operation. This changes the controller's execution path for those bus modes, avoiding use of an incompatible combined transfer path and allowing reads to proceed correctly when DUAL/QUAD nbits are requested.

grouping_result.intent: Route DUAL/QUAD SPI transfers to the proper read path instead of the combined write-read path.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the described issue by routing DUAL/QUAD SPI transfers to the proper read path instead of the write-read transmit path that incorrectly sent dummy data.

candidates.rationale: This call sends the transfer through the combined write-read path even for emulated read-only DUAL/QUAD SPI operations. Per the root cause, the driver should have used the hardware read path so the core generates the read clock cycles instead of transmitting dummy data.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call incorrectly routes emulated read-only DUAL/QUAD SPI transfers through the combined write-read path, which transmits dummy data instead of using the hardware read path to generate the necessary clock cycles.

commit 8f9cf02c8852837923f1cdacfcc92e138513325c
Author: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 20 14:28:26 2025 +0100

    spi: microchip-core-qspi: Add regular transfers
    
    The driver for CoreQSPI only supports memory operations at present, so
    add support for regular transfers so that the SD card slot and ADC on
    the BeagleV Fire can be used.
    
    Signed-off-by: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
    Co-developed-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this snippet. The bug was that emulated read-only dual/quad SPI transfers incorrectly went through the normal write-read transmit path and sent dummy data instead of letting the hardware generate read clock cycles. In this commit, the driver adds a dedicated read/write path in `mchp_coreqspi_transfer_one()` and `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op()`: for RX transfers it explicitly does `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op(qspi);` rather than reusing the plain write path (`if (!t->rx_buf) { mchp_coreqspi_write_op(qspi); } else { ... mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op(qspi); }`). The new `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op()` also enables X4 mode (`control |= CONTROL_FLAGSX4;`) and handles RX FIFO draining separately, which is the correct handling for read transfers. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent and the fix is already present in this version.
